name: PDFium
baseline: Poppler (the pdftotext command-line tool, poppler 'pdftotext' row of py-pdf/benchmarks)
workload: Text extraction from 14 pure PDFs (7 to 134 pages) via the pypdfium2 binding of PDFium against the Poppler pdftotext command, in the independent py-pdf/benchmarks suite; page rendering is not measured.
claimed_speedup: Text extraction average 0.1 s for pypdfium2 (PDFium) against 0.3 s for pdftotext (Poppler), about 3x (derived from page data, times are rounded to 0.1 s). Per document: GeoTopo-book (117 pages) 0.2 s against 1.0 s, 1707.09725 (134 pages) 0.2 s against 0.8 s, 2201.00214 0.5 s against 0.7 s, 2201.00151 0.2 s against 0.3 s. pdftotext was never faster than pypdfium2 on any of the 14 documents. Text-quality score 95% (pypdfium2) against 90% (pdftotext).
compiler_and_flags: not stated (pypdfium2 5.13.0 is a prebuilt PyPI wheel carrying a PDFium binary; pdftotext is the distribution build of Poppler, no flags given)
stars_or_usage: no GitHub star count (canonical repo is on googlesource); pdfium-binaries tracks it with release chromium/8086 (PDFium 157.0.8086.0) dated 2026-10-05
tradeoffs: Large C++ codebase with many bundled third-party dependencies (each carrying its own licence, per the pypdfium2 README), normally consumed through binary builds such as pypdfium2 or bblanchon/pdfium-binaries. Strong text extraction quality in the same suite (95% against Poppler's 90%).
caveats: Independent suite (py-pdf organisation, BSD-3-Clause, one script for every library, code public) but compiler and flags are not stated, so B not A. Not a like-for-like comparison: PDFium is driven in-process through the pypdfium2 ctypes binding (open document from bytes, get_textpage, get_text_range per page, plus Python post-processing), while Poppler is run as a subprocess (pdftotext -enc UTF-8 on a temp file written for each call), so Poppler's time includes process start and temp-file I/O, which inflates its figures on the small documents. Single run per document, no repeats, time.time(), times rounded to 0.1 s, so the 0.1 s against 0.3 s average is coarse. The measured job is text extraction (content-stream parsing and text layout), not page rasterisation, so category rasterizers-2d is a best fit (a sibling MuPDF record uses the same suite and category). The README lists pdftotext as the Python package 0.86.1 (libpoppler-cpp) but the benchmark code in library_code.py actually calls the pdftotext executable. PDFium licence taken from the list tag and the pypdfium2 README ('a BSD-style license'); pdfium.googlesource.com and its LICENSE file were not reachable from this environment. last_commit unknown for the same reason (activity inferred from pdfium-binaries releases and the pypdfium2 5.13.0 release of 2026-08-13). Other PDFium-versus-Poppler rendering comparisons exist (PDF Association 2021 Survey of OpenSource Solutions, Alfresco blog) but pdfa.org and hub.alfresco.com are blocked here and were not read.

name: Poppler
baseline: pdfminer.six (pure-Python PDF text extractor; pypdf and pdfplumber are also in the table)
workload: Text extraction from 14 pure PDFs (7 to 134 pages) with the Poppler pdftotext command against pure-Python extractors, in the independent py-pdf/benchmarks suite; page rendering is not measured.
claimed_speedup: Text extraction average 0.3 s for pdftotext (Poppler) against 5.5 s for pdfminer.six (about 18x), 3.3 s for pypdf (about 11x) and 8.6 s for pdfplumber (about 29x), ratios derived from page data. Per document: GeoTopo-book (117 pages) 1.0 s against 14.0 s for pdfminer.six; 2201.00214 0.7 s against 34.3 s; 1707.09725 (134 pages) 0.8 s against 5.4 s. Text-quality score 90% for pdftotext against 88% (pdfminer.six) and 95% (pypdf).
compiler_and_flags: not stated (distribution build of pdftotext from Poppler, no flags given; pdfminer.six 20260107, pypdf 6.19.0, pdfplumber 0.11.10)
stars_or_usage: no GitHub star count (canonical repo is on gitlab.freedesktop.org); the suite's table links pdftotext to poppler.freedesktop.org
tradeoffs: GPL (list tag GPLv2/GPLv3) copyleft, so linking it into permissive or closed products is restricted. The fast path in this suite is the command-line tool, not the library API.
caveats: The headline wins are over pure-Python libraries, a weak baseline, and Poppler is not the fastest engine in the same table: pypdfium2 (PDFium) averages 0.1 s and PyMuPDF (MuPDF) 0.1 s, about 3x faster than pdftotext. Independent suite (py-pdf organisation, BSD-3-Clause, code public) but compiler and flags not stated, so B not A. The Poppler number includes process start and a temp-file write for each document (pdftotext is run as a subprocess in library_code.py), so it understates in-process library speed. Single run per document, no repeats, times rounded to 0.1 s. Measured job is text extraction, not rasterisation. Licence taken from the list tag; poppler.freedesktop.org and gitlab.freedesktop.org were not reachable from this environment (blocked), so last_commit and stars are unknown. Maintenance inferred from a search snippet of the releases page (poppler 26.08.0 dated 2026-08-02, 26.07.0 dated 2026-07-02), not from an opened page. Rendering comparisons against MuPDF, PDFium and Ghostscript (PDF Association 2021 survey, Alfresco blog) were not readable (hosts blocked).
